newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Lack of rain delays plantings in key Brazil state.
newsitem.headline: Lack of rain delays plantings in key Brazil state.

text.p: Wheat plantings in Brazil's key state of Parana were only 22 percent completed by May 9 against 35 percent by the same stage last year, said an agronomist at the State Agricultural Secretariat.
Normally plantings at this stage would be between 35 and 40 percent finished, added Otmar Hubner.
The delay in plantings is due to dry weather and is particularly hitting the north of the state where normally all the crop would be sowed by May 20.
Up to May 9, only 60 percent of seeds were in the ground, Hubner said.
"The planting period can be extended for 10 more days so if there is some rain they can still finish it in time," he said.
State output is expected to reach between 1.75 million and 1.92 million tonnes, down from last year's crop of just over two million tonnes.
Independent consultants Safras e Mercado forecast in mid-April that the national crop should reach around 2.52 million tonnes against 3.13 million in 1996.
